observation.visible_scene: A split air–water view filmed at the surface of a wave, looking upward toward a bright sun in the upper-right sky. Below the undulating waterline is turbulent, refracted underwater light with a dark-green wave face on the left; above it is blue sky with faint clouds and a dark, jagged band (reflection/crest silhouette) running along the surface. Small bright dots (droplets or bubbles) float near the sun.
visible_changes: The water-surface boundary tilts and settles over the excerpt: on the left it drops from a high position toward mid-frame, making the line less steep, while the right end stays roughly level — consistent with a slow camera roll/bob combined with wave motion rather than independent object movement.
The dark jagged band along the surface continuously deforms, spreading horizontally and drifting slightly rightward, its silhouette reshaping from frame to frame.
The underwater region shows constantly shifting caustic/refraction patterns; the green wave face on the left changes shape and extent.
The sun and glare persist in the upper-right throughout, with the small bright dots moving only slightly; the sky/cloud reflection above the line shifts as the surface moves.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the dark jagged band actually represents (a reflection of a distant object, a breaking crest, or a silhouette) is not determined.
The cause of the camera's tilt/bob and the wave's formation before this segment, and the outcome after it, are unseen.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent leftward/rightward drift of the surface line is camera motion, wave motion, or both, since the whole scene shifts together.
Whether the small bright dots are airborne droplets, underwater bubbles, or lens artifacts.
Whether the dark band is a separate object or a reflection of the sky/crest.
